seoTitle: Free Query String Parser and Builder Online
metaDescription: Parse a URL query string into key and value pairs and JSON, or build one from key=value lines or JSON. Free, handles repeated keys, runs in your browser.
intro: Parse a query string or full URL into key/value pairs and JSON, or build a properly encoded query string from lines of key=value or from a JSON object.
why:
Query strings carry search filters, campaign tags, API parameters and OAuth state, and they get messy: repeated keys, plus signs for spaces, nested JSON in a value. Reading them in a raw URL is a chore, and building one by hand means remembering which characters to encode.

In parse mode this tool lists every pair, numbered, and gives a JSON view where repeated keys become arrays. In build mode it takes key=value lines or a JSON object and creates an encoded string, with spaces as %20 or +. Arrays turn into repeated keys, and nested objects are written as JSON text. It runs in your browser.
howTo: Choose a mode: parse or build.
For parse, paste a URL or just the part after the question mark. For build, paste key=value lines or a JSON object.
For build, pick whether spaces become %20 or +.
Copy the pairs, the JSON or the finished query string.

faq.a: When parsing, the JSON view turns repeated keys into an array in order. When building from JSON, an array value becomes repeated keys, such as tag=a&tag=b. This is the most widely understood convention.
Both are accepted in form-encoded query strings, but only %20 is valid anywhere in a URL. Choose + when mimicking an HTML form. If unsure, keep %20.

faq.q: What happens with nested objects in JSON?
faq.a: Objects inside values are converted to JSON text and then encoded, since there is no universal standard for nesting in query strings. Servers using bracket syntax such as a[b]=1 need those keys written in the lines mode.

faq.q: Does it decode percent-encoding when parsing?
faq.a: Yes. Keys and values are decoded, and plus signs are read as spaces, as for form data. Use the URL Decode tool for a plain decode of other text.
